claims.statement: The backend money model uses two representations: raw numeric values (prices, position quantity and average_cost) are `Decimal` in the API types, while any currency-tagged amount is `stockholm.Money`; `Account.currency` and `Security.currency` are `stockholm.currency.Currency`, but read models downgrade currency to plain `str` (`HoldingRead.currency`, `AccountHoldingsRead.currency`, `AccountHoldingRead.currency`) and `AccountSchema` uses an explicit `@field_serializer("currency")` to emit its `Currency` as a code string, so `Currency` survives only in the service layer and the write path.

A `stockholm.Money` serializes to JSON as a single currency-suffixed string field (for example `{"value": "500.00 USD"}`), not as structured `units`/`nanos`/`currencyCode`; tests assert `payload["totals"]["cost"]["value"] == "500.00 USD"` and that `result["cost"]["value"]` ends with `" CAD"`.

Currency conversion inside the position math is centralized in `PositionService._currency_convert`, which short-circuits when the source and target currency codes match and otherwise calls `currency_converter.CurrencyConverter.convert(...)`, rounds the result to 2 decimal places, and re-wraps it as `Money`; the converter is supplied by `FxRateProvider` — `position_service_factory` resolves the provider and passes `fx_rates=await fx_provider.converter()` — rather than being constructed by the service itself.

Conversion is applied per position before accumulation rather than to stored values, so positions never have their `average_cost` rewritten by FX and every accumulator for total cost, total value, and total P&L adds only account-currency `Money` values.

`HoldingRead` reports the same logical amount up to three times — native values under `security_currency` (`unconverted_total_value`, `average_cost`, `latest_price`, `unconverted_profit_loss`), account-currency values under `currency` (`total_value`, `profit_loss`, `converted_average_cost`, `converted_latest_price`), and a display pair (`display_total_value`/`display_currency`) — and the holdings tables print the second line only when `holding.security_currency !== holding.currency`; `security_currency` is actually `position.currency or security.currency`, `unconverted_total_value` is the native value converted into that position currency, and `latest_price` stays the raw security-currency close.

`AccountTotals` is served by `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` — which accepts an optional `currency` query parameter validated against `SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_CURRENCIES` and returning 422 for anything else — and pushed over WebSocket as `AccountTotalsUpdatedMessage` by the `recalculate_all_account_totals_task` Huey task, which calls `get_total_for_account(account.id, account.currency)` once per active account inside a per-account `try/except`; the frontend does not listen for that message, since `accounts-list.svelte.ts` handles only `sync_started`/`sync_finished`/`sync_failed` and `websocket.ts` does not even declare the totals event, so the account list still fetches totals over HTTP and caches them per account.

When `account.net_deposits` is not `None`, `_account_performance` sets `basis = "net_deposits"` and `profit_loss = value - net_deposits` (a cash-flow P&L, not a cost-basis figure) with `return_percent` reported only when `net_deposits != 0`; because `get_account_holdings` and `get_total_for_account` both go through that helper, `AccountHoldingsRead.total_profit_loss`/`total_profit_loss_percent`/`profit_loss_basis` agree with `AccountTotals`, and the asset test asserts `total_value == 1500`, `total_profit_loss == 500` and `total_profit_loss_percent == 50.0` for `1500 - 1000`.

The frontend `Money` interface is `{ value?: string; units?: number; nanos?: number; currencyCode?: string }`, and `moneyToNumber` prefers `units + nanos / 1e9` when `units` is a number, otherwise falls back to `parseFloat(value)`, returning `0` for null, undefined, or unparseable input; `money(m)` renders `$<localized number>`.

Because the API emits `value` strings like `"500.00 CAD"` with no `units`, the `units`/`nanos` branch of `moneyToNumber` is unused against the live backend and real responses succeed only because `parseFloat` stops at the first non-numeric character; the frontend fixtures disagree with each other — `accounts-list-item.test.ts` and `total-profit-loss-buttons.test.ts` supply `units`/`nanos` alongside `value` while `account-totals.test.ts` builds `{ value: '0', currencyCode: 'CAD' }` with none — so the units path only looks alive in some tests, and a serializer or parser change on either side must update both the backend shape and the frontend `Money` type together or amounts silently become wrong or `0`.

`blendedAverageCost` computes the quantity-weighted mean of `average_cost` across holdings, returning `0` for an empty list, zero total quantity, or all-missing costs, and treating a missing `average_cost` as `0` so an unknown-cost holding pulls the blended figure toward zero rather than being excluded.

Holdings period math runs on JS `number`: `getBenchmarkPrice` returns the average cost for `period === 'ALL'` and otherwise the close of the most recent candle at or before the period cutoff (falling back to the earliest candle), and `calculateHoldingGain` returns `gainAmount = (currentPrice - benchmarkPrice) * quantity` and `gainPercent = priceDiff / benchmarkPrice * 100` guarded to `0` when the benchmark is `0`.

Precision is lost at defined storage boundaries: `PositionModel.quantity` is `DECIMAL(16, 8)` but `PositionModel.average_cost` is `Float` and `PositionModel.currency` a nullable `String(3)`, `AccountModel.currency` is a plain `String` (while the service-layer API type is `Currency`), and `AccountModel.net_deposits` and `AccountModel.free_cash` are `Float`, so cash-flow P&L and the cash contribution to both totals inherit float error.

`src/account/csv/parser.py` parses quantities and book values as `Decimal` after stripping `,` and `$`, and computes `average_cost` as `(book_value / quantity).quantize(Decimal("0.0001"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)`, returning `None` for non-positive quantity or missing book value.

`get_holdings_by_security` computes `account_percentage` from `MarketPricesApi.get_latest_close` multiplied by quantity, rounded to 2 places, converted to the account currency, then divided by `get_total_for_account(...).value.amount` (a denominator that already includes `free_cash`), reporting the percentage only when that denominator is positive; the same rounded native value is converted a second time into `display_currency`, defaulting to the account currency, for `display_total_value`.

CSV import currency selection and update affect aggregates: `chosen_currency` is the trimmed, upper-cased per-account value from the import request, else the currency the CSV parser derived (which itself falls back to `CAD` when a row carries no currency column and no `book_value_currency_*`/`market_price_currency` value), else `CAD`; an existing account's currency is updated when it differs from `chosen_currency`, and new accounts are created with `currency=Currency(chosen_currency)`.

The `account_totals_success` router test exercises `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` and asserts that the returned `cost`, `value`, `cash` and `profit_loss` money strings carry the ` CAD` suffix plus the presence of `net_deposits` and `return_percent` and `basis == "cost"`; `test_account_totals_converts_to_requested_currency` asserts `?currency=USD` converts the same fields, `test_account_totals_unsupported_currency_returns_422` rejects an unknown code, and `test_account_totals_not_found` / `test_account_totals_not_owned` assert 404 rather than a currency payload.

Because the FX conversion target is the account's own `currency` (passed as `account.currency` into every `_currency_convert` call site in the position math), changing an account's currency re-bases every converted total, value, and P&L for that account without modifying any stored position; CSV import is one path that does this, updating an existing account's currency when a different `chosen_currency` is supplied.

`account.free_cash`, wrapped as `Money(free_cash, account.currency)` and converted, is added to both `AccountTotals.cost` and `AccountTotals.value` in `_account_performance`, so reported totals and the cash-flow P&L include cash and `AccountTotals.cost` stops being a pure cost basis once cash is non-zero — which also means every consumer of `AccountTotals.value`, including `get_holdings_by_security`'s `account_percentage` denominator and the `/holdings` per-currency header buckets, is measuring cash plus holdings.

Per-position products are rounded to 2 decimal places before conversion or accumulation: `_calculate_holding` rounds `quantity × latest close` and `quantity × average_cost` in the native currency, `get_holdings_by_security` rounds `quantity × latest close` before converting, and `_currency_convert` rounds each converted amount before accumulation, so every aggregate is a sum of rounded per-position values rather than the rounded sum of exact values.

Missing prices and missing FX rates fail differently. A missing stored price is an explicit, counted gap: `_calculate_holdings` increments `unpriced_positions`, appends an `_unpriced_holding` row with `profit_loss = None` and `total_value = 0.0`, and excludes the position from both `positions_cost` and `positions_value`, so the totals understate the account and `pricing_incomplete` becomes `True`; a `SecurityNotFoundError` is caught per position, logged, and counted the same way, while `get_holdings_by_security` instead falls back to `latest_price = 0.0` and returns `([], 0)` for an unknown security. A missing FX rate pair is not handled at all: `_currency_convert` has no fallback and lets the `currencyconverter` error propagate, so `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` fails the request while `_recalculate_all_account_totals` catches per account, logs, and continues.

`total-profit-loss-buttons.svelte` is the live renderer for account totals: it converts its `Money | number` props with `moneyToNumber`, keeps the caller-supplied `costBasis` separate from the derived `cost` (`value - profitLoss`), derives the return percentage as `(profitLoss / cost) * 100` when not supplied but honours an explicit `returnPercent: null` as "no percent", and formats with `Intl.NumberFormat('en-CA', { style: 'currency', currency })`; the `money()` helper in `money.ts` renders a bare `$` with no currency code and no fixed decimals and has no production caller (only tests import it), while the holdings views use the same explicit-currency `Intl.NumberFormat` helper because they mix security and account currencies.

`holding-group.svelte` normalizes before dividing: it fetches every account's totals in the user's display currency (`getAccountTotals(acc.id, undefined, displayCurrency)`, with the preference defaulting to `CAD`) and divides the sum of the security's `display_total_value` rows by that sum, so numerator and denominator share one currency while the denominator still includes each account's `free_cash`.

Market price columns are fixed-point: `PriceModel` and `IntradayPriceModel` store `open`, `high`, `low`, `close` (and `adjusted_close` on `PriceModel`) as `DECIMAL(16, 8)`, and user-entered price fields share that convention — `PriceAlertModel.target_price` and `SecurityValuationModel`/`SecurityValuationHistoryModel` `lower_bound`/`upper_bound` are also `DECIMAL(16, 8)` — while their write schemas (`PriceAlertWrite.target_price`, `SecurityValuationWrite.lower_bound`/`upper_bound`) accept an unconstrained `Decimal` and the frontend `ValuationClient` types both valuation bounds as plain `number`, so 8 fractional digits is the effective precision and the database, not validation, rounds anything more precise.

`holdings-metrics.ts` also owns the holdings-table ratio helpers: `calculatePercentOfTotal` and `calculatePercentOfAccount` both return `0` for non-finite inputs or a non-positive denominator, and `formatHoldingPercent` renders one decimal place or `-` for null/non-finite values, so these ratios are always plain JS `number` derived from float-typed `HoldingRead` fields.

`blendedAverageCost` has three production consumers, not one: `holding-group.svelte` (the "Average" row, formatted `en-US`), the `holdings-modal.svelte` footer `portfolioAvgPrice`, and the security detail page's `averageBuyingPrice`, which feeds the chart's average-price overlay line via `security-chart.svelte`'s `averagePrice` prop.

The cross-account holdings page never sums across currencies: `frontend/src/routes/holdings/+page.svelte` collects the visible accounts' server `AccountTotals` (fetched in each account's own currency) and calls `aggregateAccountTotals` in `frontend/src/lib/utils/finance/account-totals.ts`, which buckets by `currency` and sums `value` and `profit_loss` per bucket, using `sum(net_deposits)` as the return denominator only when every account in the bucket reports basis `net_deposits` and otherwise `sum(value) - sum(profit_loss)` labelled "mixed basis" with `basisAmount: null`, and yields `returnPercent: null` for a zero denominator — the pattern any new cross-account aggregate should copy.

The watchlist surfaces deliberately render no currency symbol: `watchlist-utils.ts` exposes `formatPrice` (2 decimals, `-` for absent or unparseable) and `formatPriceChangePercent` (signed 2 decimals, `0.00%` for zero and negative zero), and `watchlists/+page.svelte` renders `SecuritySchema.current_price` and `daily_price_change_percent` through them; the module also carries its own object-shaped `formatValuationRange` accepting `number | string` bounds, separate from the `$lib/utils/finance/valuation` variant the holdings table uses.

Only the cross-account holdings table owns the valuation-range column: `frontend/src/lib/components/holdings/holdings-table.svelte` formats `row.valuation_lower`/`valuation_upper` with `formatValuationRange` from `$lib/utils/finance/valuation`, whereas the account-scoped `frontend/src/lib/components/accounts/holdings-table.svelte` has no valuation column at all — so the range-formatting contract lives on the cross-account surface.

`total-profit-loss-buttons.svelte` falls back to a signed `$x.xx` string when `Intl.NumberFormat` rejects the currency code, and although its `effectiveCurrency` derivation contains a `Money.currencyCode` fallback, the `currency` prop defaults to `'CAD'`, so the display currency is in practice whichever currency the caller passes (the account list passes `account.currency`, the `/holdings` header passes the bucket currency).

`_account_performance` is the single place that decides what P/L means and composes `AccountTotals`: `cash` is `account.free_cash` converted into the target currency and is added to both `cost` (the converted positions cost basis) and `value` (the converted positions market value); when `net_deposits` is known the basis is `net_deposits` with `profit_loss = value - net_deposits`, otherwise the basis is `cost` with `profit_loss = positions_value - positions_cost`, so cash is deliberately excluded from the cost-basis ratio; and `return_percent` is `None` when the chosen denominator is zero.

`_unpriced_holding` surfaces a position with no stored price as a real row — `total_value = 0.0`, `profit_loss = None`, `unconverted_total_value = 0.0`, `latest_price = None`, `price_date = None`, but a real converted `converted_average_cost` and the position/account currency pair — while `_calculate_holdings` keeps it out of `total_value` and `total_cost`, so the position stays visible with its cost basis without corrupting the account totals.

Both holdings endpoints convert a second time into the user's display currency: `/accounts/holdings` and `/accounts/holdings/{security_id}` pass `await user_api.get_display_currency(user.id)` into `PositionService`, `UserApi.get_display_currency` reads the persisted `display_currency` preference and defaults to `CAD`, and that preference is validated against `SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_CURRENCIES = ("CAD", "USD", "EUR", "GBP")` on write, so `display_total_value`/`display_currency` are always expressed in one of those codes.

The `CurrencyConverter` used for FX is built by `FxRateProvider.converter()`: it parses the ECB history zip that the daily Huey periodic task `daily_fx_refresh` stores in Redis (`refresh_fx_rates` writes the base64 zip and its fetch-date key atomically with `MSET`), caches the parsed converter at module level keyed by fetch date (bounded, with per-event-loop build locks and negative caching of an unparseable zip), and falls back to the bundled `currencyconverter` snapshot when Redis is unreachable, empty, or holds a corrupt zip — so a converter is always available and "missing FX data" surfaces as a stale rate (warned once it is more than 3 business days old) rather than as an exception.

Broker sync is the only other FX consumer: `_sum_cash_in_account_currency` (`src/integration/task.py`) converts each reported cash balance into the account currency through the same `FxRateProvider` converter, accumulating in `float` because the converters are not built with `decimal=True`, and rounds to 2 places before writing `free_cash`; gateways that cannot report cash inherit the base no-op and leave `free_cash` untouched.

Listing currency is a separate concept from account currency: `resolve_listing_currency` (`src/market/currency.py`) resolves a quote's unit from the company profile normalized by `normalize_currency` (blank or `None` → `None`, `GBp`/`GBX` → `GBX`, everything else upper-cased) with a deterministic `EXCHANGE_DEFAULT_CURRENCY` fallback (`TSX` → `CAD`, `LSE` → `GBX`, US venues and `None` → `USD`) and an `or "USD"` catch-all, caching the result under data class `metrics` / endpoint `listing_currency`; it only labels price-bearing data-plane responses and never changes `Account.currency`, positions, or account totals.

`frontend/src/lib/components/holdings/holdings-table.svelte` computes `% of Total` and the per-account badges from `display_total_value` — the value the backend already converted into the user's display currency — rather than from the native `total_value`, so a CAD row and a USD row are compared in one currency and the percentages are not a naive native-units ratio.

`accounts-list-item.svelte` renders the server's `AccountTotals` verbatim — `totalValue={totals.value}`, `costBasis` set to `totals.net_deposits` when `basis === 'net_deposits'` and to `totals.cost` otherwise, plus the server `profit_loss` and `return_percent` — so no browser-side `value - cost` P&L remains in the account list, and it shows the amber incomplete-pricing warning when `totals.pricing_incomplete`.

The three holdings surfaces derive per-row P&L percentages differently: `accounts/holdings-table.svelte` uses `profit_loss / (quantity * (converted_average_cost ?? 0)) * 100` guarded by `average_cost > 0`, while `account-inline-holdings.svelte` and `holdings/holdings-table.svelte` use `profit_loss / (quantity * (converted_average_cost ?? average_cost ?? 0)) * 100` and skip a non-positive cost basis — so the account-scoped variant divides by zero and renders `Infinity`/`NaN` when the converted cost is missing while `average_cost` is present.

`get_account_holdings` computes the header totals over all of the account's positions via `_calculate_holdings` and then re-reads the paginated page for `items`, so the totals cover positions outside the current page and, because both paths share the same calculation loop, `get_total_for_account` and `get_account_holdings` report identical `value`, `profit_loss`, `return_percent` and basis.
